### CPU cache
Part 1 of 2

A CPU cache is small, fast memory near processor cores that keeps copies of recently or nearby used data and instructions. Locality can reduce slower RAM accesses. L1 is typically smaller and closer than L2 or L3; sizes and sharing vary by processor. A cache miss costs time, but cache size alone does not predict application speed.

### CPU versus GPU
A CPU handles general program execution; a GPU specializes in highly parallel work such as rendering. Workloads vary, so neither is simply a universal replacement for the other.

Reference: [CPU versus GPU](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web). Reviewed 2026-10-24.

### SSD storage
An SSD is nonvolatile storage: it retains files when power is removed. RAM holds active program data and is normally volatile. SSD latency is much higher than RAM latency, so adding SSD capacity does not replace adequate RAM. Flash write endurance and interface speed vary; an SSD is not a backup.

Reference: [SSD storage](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/solid-state-drives). Reviewed 2026-10-26.

### WebAssembly
WebAssembly is a compact code format designed for portable execution. In a browser it operates within sandbox and API constraints; it does not grant unrestricted system access.

Reference: [WebAssembly](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web). Reviewed 2026-10-24.

| WebAssembly | Portable sandboxed code format | Usually CPU, with optional SIMD/threads when supported | Runs CPU inference kernels and supports fallback when GPU execution is unavailable\. |
